fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the road entrance to the driveway so responders can locate the property quickly from the street.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the access point at night or in low visibility.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the driveway so a full-size fire or rescue vehicle can travel its full length without obstruction.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and debris so responding units can reach the residence without delay.
• Designate and mark a turnaround area near the residence or detached structure so large vehicles can reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Post the address number visibly at both the road and the main residence so responders can confirm they have reached the correct structure.
• Mark or sign the detached structure with its relationship to the main residence so responders arriving on scene understand the site layout immediately.
• Clear a path between the main residence and the detached structure wide enough for responders carrying equipment to move between the two buildings.
• Trim dense vegetation back from both sides of the access drive to maintain clear sightlines for drivers and to prevent vegetation from slowing vehicle movement.
• Keep a gate or access point to the patio area unlocked or fitted with a lockbox so responders can reach that side of the residence without forcing entry

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees in the cluster closest to the structure to create open space between the canopy and the building.
• Thin trees in the second cluster near the structure to reduce the amount of continuous tree cover surrounding the building.
• Trim branches on the large trees that extend directly over or toward the structure.
• Remove shrubs and low-growing plants that are in direct contact with or immediately next to the structure walls.
• Clear ground vegetation growing against the base of the structure on all visible sides.
• Separate shrubs from the structure by removing or relocating those within a few feet of the foundation.
• Thin scattered shrubs across the property to break up the continuous vegetation surrounding the structure.
• Trim overhanging branches along the full length of the driveway so vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Clear shrubs and ground vegetation growing along the edges of the driveway to keep the travel lane open.
• Keep the driveway surface free of fallen branches, dead leaves, and other debris that could block vehicle movement.
• Remove dead plant material from around the base of trees and shrubs near the structure.
• Keep the single access route clear at all times, as it is the only way in and out for residents and emergency vehicles.
